entry_state: Aggregation can leave both movement amounts and economically important contract terms unidentified. Balanced batches conserve a signed functional-currency book, but reporting also needs classified movements, economic state, basis and perimeter. Future simulation must therefore generate economic events and apply accounting treatment rather than evolve statement totals alone.
exit_state: Simulation separates permitted actions, economic events, accounting treatment and atomic state transitions. Conditional report laws remain a family unless a justified measure over histories is supplied; mixture, variance and weight-set bounds have distinct assumptions. Grouping requires equal requested conditional laws, and sampled extrema remain inner exploration. One local notation defect is confirmed: theta in the simulation equations is never defined.
findings: Equations 6.4–6.7 distinguish policy, event generation, accounting and state transition. The default example makes their separate financial effects concrete, and nested measurement cannot use the realised future path.

Theta is used after the semicolon in the policy and event equations but has no prose definition. A source-wide search finds only these two uses; the defect concerns reconstructing the parameter role, not an established wrong mathematical identity.

Equation 6.9 supplies measurable-space and probability-kernel assumptions before mixing histories. Finite illustrative weights, total variance and lower/upper probabilities retain their separate meanings.
The grouping relation depends on requested outputs, horizon and scenarios. Sampled extrema are distinguished from certified bounds and interval outer bounds.

defects.evidence: Equations 6.4 and 6.5 use theta in pi and G. The preceding paragraph defines X, s, U, a, epsilon and the permitted information but not theta; the following explanation also omits it. A search of all candidate TeX sources returns only the two equation occurrences. The reader must guess its parameter role and whether it is part of the declared history/scenario assumptions.
defects.repair: Before the aligned simulation display, define theta's role in behavioural policy and event generation and state how its declared values relate to the chosen history/scenario/model assumptions. Preserve all equations and avoid inventing fitted values or claiming a calibrated policy.
defects.disposition: Repair trigger after the complete fixed-candidate diagnosis; no continuation veto and no mathematical incorrectness verdict established by this notation finding.
